themes.name: Critical Thinking in AI-Integrated Education
themes.definition: The development and enhancement of critical thinking skills through structured integration of AI tools across diverse educational contexts, emphasizing evaluation of AI-generated outputs and problem-solving.
evidence: [Maya2024] Students reported significant improvement in critical thinking skills (Mean = 3.82, SD = 0.86)
[Malang2025] ChatGPT supports students in understanding complex concepts, improving writing and critical thinking skills
[Han2025b] Foster the development of critical and creative thinking skills among learners

themes.name: Generative AI in Language/Writing Instruction
themes.definition: Application of generative AI tools to improve disciplinary literacy, academic writing quality, and language acquisition through multimodal scaffolding and collaborative frameworks.
evidence: [Sánchez-Fortún2026] Significant improvements observed in textual coherence, grammatical accuracy, and integration of visual elements
[Yang2024] Six-step human-AI hybrid framework enhanced prompt engineering techniques and critical assessment of AI responses
[Chen2025f] Gen AI influences cognitive processes like reflection and critical thinking in inquiry-based language learning

themes.name: Pedagogical Strategies for AI Integration
themes.definition: Structured methodologies combining AI tools with traditional educational frameworks to optimize learning outcomes, including BOPPPS model, TPACK framework, and dual-report assessments.
evidence: [Han2025b] Integrated generative AI with BOPPPS instructional design to stimulate deep thinking
[Ravi2025] TPACK framework for designing AI-enabled learning activities that foster critical thinking
[Browning2024] Dual-report assessment evaluates both project outcomes and students' prompt engineering proficiency

themes.name: Ethical and Reliability Considerations
themes.definition: Challenges relating to academic integrity, critical evaluation of AI outputs, and ethical use of AI tools as emphasized in both qualitative reflections and quantitative surveys.
evidence: [Camarillo2025] Students recognized GenAI's ethical limitations despite its information access advantages
[Alexander2025] Emphasis on ethical use of ChatGPT and critical reflection of its implications
[Rachmat2025] Students perceived chatbots as unreliable due to hallucinations and inaccurate code snippets

themes.name: Technology-Induced Learning Challenges
themes.definition: Emerging issues such as reduced peer discussion, initial anxiety about AI literacy, and varying effectiveness of AI tools across disciplines and learner demographics.
evidence: [Kim2023] Overreliance on ChatGPT leading to reduced discussions
[Huang2024] Concerns about reduced academic integrity fears
[Lu2025] Over-reliance on AI-generated content may weaken higher-order thinking skills

data.meta_observations: Emergent themes heavily focus on critical thinking enhancement, with generative AI serving as both facilitator and object of critical analysis. Language/writing emerges as the most experimentally adopted field for AI integration. Ethical considerations remain secondary to skill-focused outcomes. Methodological rigor varies significantly across abstracts, with many lacking quantitative results or conclusions.
data.grounding_notes: All themes strictly derive from explicit data. Some articles (e.g., Han2026, Zakirova2025) contribute to critical thinking themes but were excluded due to weaker direct terminology. High confidence in most themes; technology-induced challenges has lower confidence due to limited explicit mentions.
